cards.explanation: The answer is that they take as wives whomever they choose. The text says the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and "…they took as wives whomever they chose." Notice the choosing was all theirs, friends. The passage doesn't say anyone else got a vote (Genesis 6:2).

The answer is 120 years. The LORD says, "My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years" (Genesis 6:3). Just a few verses back, Methuselah, Enoch's son, lived 969 years (Genesis 5:27). So 120 is a number you notice right after all those long ones. The verse doesn't say more than what the LORD says here, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is wickedness. "Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth…" (Genesis 6:5). The verse keeps going and says every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time. I think this is one of the hard spots in the passage, friends. The LORD sees all of it, and I'd rather read it slowly than rush past it.

The answer is False. The text says "…every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time" (Genesis 6:5). Not some of the time, friends, all the time. So False is the one that matches the verse.

The answer is True. The text says, "…the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart" (Genesis 6:6). Both parts are right there in the same verse, friends. This one hurts to read, so I'll just let it sit for a moment.

The answer is that He will blot out man from the earth. The LORD says, "I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth…" (Genesis 6:7). Then He adds that He is grieved that He made them. I think that's the part to sit with, friends. The text says He was grieved in His heart (Genesis 6:6), and that makes this verse hit harder.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air…" (Genesis 6:7). The list goes past man to the animals too, friends. It's a long list, and the verse doesn't hurry through it.

The answer is Noah. "Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD" (Genesis 6:8). That little word "however" turns the whole verse around, friends. After all that heavy news, here's one man the text sets apart.
